purpose: Create an approved international English master from Simplified Chinese. This master is the only source for every later locale.
semanticContract: Simplified Chinese is the final factual authority.
Do not add, remove, weaken, broaden, narrow, or substitute features, audiences, guarantees, comparisons, conditions, limitations, prices, or commercial claims.
When the Chinese source is ambiguous, retain the ambiguity or mark it for human review; never invent a more marketable interpretation.
Brand names, product names, prices, currencies, dates, quantities, URLs, emails, variables, code, identifiers, and technical limits must remain exact.
internationalEnglish: Use globally understood contemporary English. Avoid region-specific slang, idioms, spelling, date formats, units, and cultural references unless the source page is market-specific.
Prefer direct active sentences and concrete verbs. Keep one primary idea per sentence.
Use sentence case for headings and navigation labels unless an established brand or UI convention requires otherwise.
Use short, action-oriented CTAs that match the real action: Download, Get started, Learn more, View plans, Contact us, or equivalent.
Use clear noun phrases or verb phrases for feature cards; never use past-tense release-note phrasing as a feature name.
Keep terminology consistent across every page and module.
grammarAndStyleChecks: Check subject-verb agreement, articles, countable nouns, singular/plural form, pronoun reference, prepositions, tense, capitalization, punctuation, and parallel structure.
Do not translate Chinese four-character slogans, paired phrases, or abstract business nouns literally. Rebuild the sentence around the product capability or user outcome.

Avoid vague filler and unsupported superlatives, including empower, revolutionary, world-class, industry-leading, global enabler, experience now, more convenient, realize a feature, and setting an industry benchmark.
Do not use title case by default. Do not add a period to a short button label.
Use a glossary-approved term for each product concept; do not vary terms for stylistic reasons.
referenceUse: Comparable English-language product websites may guide information hierarchy, headline density, CTA patterns, and plain-language rhythm.
They cannot supply facts, claims, terminology, or wording for VicastCam. Never copy their copy.
reviewQuestions: Does this sound like original international consumer-tech website copy rather than translated Chinese?
Does every source fact and limitation remain present and unchanged?
Are all headline, CTA, and feature labels specific, concise, and consistent?
Could a non-native reader misread a product claim, a condition, a price, or a technical limit?
